overall: The AG found the Medfield School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law in drafting and issuing its February 11 mask-wearing statement, because the Chair and Superintendent were not a quorum; it declined to rule on the Chair's authority.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee deliberated outside a properly noticed meeting to draft and disseminate a February 11 statement on mask wearing.
allegations.key_passage: Absent sufficient evidence to the contrary, we credit the Committee’s account of events and find that here, where the Chair and the Superintendent do not constitute a quorum of the Committee, the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a noticed meeting regarding the Statement.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair lacked authority to issue the statement on the committee's behalf without the committee's prior approval.
allegations.key_passage: we therefore decline to opine on the Chair’s authority in this regard.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged members met or communicated on February 11 after a 9:30 a.m. meeting was canceled, citing a member's remark to a resident.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, Mr. Knight has confirmed that he did not meet with any other Committee member on February 11 and did not communicate with any Committee member regarding the Statement.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
